Accordingly, the revised timelines for completion of the various activ
rows.summary:
SEBI has introduced a new, faster rights issue framework through the **SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) (Amendment) Regulations, 2025**, notified in the Official Gazette on **March 8, 2025** (Gazette ID **CG-DL-E-08032025-261516**), and implemented through Circular **SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2025/31 dated March 11, 2025**. The key substantive change is that **all rights issues must now be completed within 23 working days from the date the issuer’s Board of Directors approves the rights issue**. This shortened timetable applies to the entire rights issue process and is intended to speed up execution by compressing the regulatory and operational steps involved.

The circular is addressed to **listed entities, recognized stock exchanges, recognized depositories, registered registrars to an issue and share transfer agents, registered bankers to an issue, self-certified syndicate banks (SCSBs), and the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI)**, so compliance obligations are not limited to issuers alone; all market infrastructure and service participants involved in the rights issue process must align their internal procedures to the new accelerated schedule. SEBI states that, as part of the amended framework, it has revised the timelines for completion of the various activities in a rights issue, meaning participants must follow the updated milestone deadlines issued under the circular rather than legacy timelines.

The new framework also adds **flexibility in allotment to specific investor(s)**, which is the principal feature highlighted in the circular title. For compliance purposes, this means rights issues may be structured with the ability to direct allotment to identified investors within the parameters of the amended ICDR regime, so issuers and intermediaries must ensure that allocation, documentation, disclosures, and processing are consistent with the revised rules before launching a rights issue. The NSE circular simply forwards SEBI’s circular for information and necessary action and notes that the SEBI circular is available on the NSE website.

rows.title: Circular on the Industry Standards Note on Key Performance Indicators (“KPIs”) Disclosures in the draft Offer Document and Offer Document
rows.summary:
This circular communicates SEBI’s adoption of an Industry Standards Note governing how Key Performance Indicators (“KPIs”) must be identified and disclosed in a draft offer document and the final offer document for securities offerings. It is addressed to all listed entities, proposed-to-be-listed entities, recognized stock exchanges, registered merchant bankers, and the three industry bodies that formed the Industry Standards Forum (ASSOCHAM, FICCI, and CII). The purpose is to create a uniform approach to KPI identification and disclosure practices, so issuers and their advisors must align offer-document preparation with the new industry standard rather than relying on ad hoc presentation of KPIs.

For compliance teams, the operative change is that KPI disclosures in draft offer documents and offer documents must follow the SEBI-referenced Industry Standards Note enclosed with the circular. This means the issuer and merchant banker involved in a public issue/offer must review the standard and ensure the KPI information included in the document is prepared and presented in accordance with that framework. The NSE circular states that the SEBI circular dated February 28, 2025 and the accompanying Industry Standards Note are enclosed and also available on the NSE website, indicating that the standard is effective from that date unless the enclosed standard specifies a later implementation date.

The document does not, in the excerpt provided, specify any numeric thresholds, KPI formulas, or filing deadlines beyond the circular date of February 28, 2025. It also does not set out a separate exemption process or special procedure in the excerpt; rather, it imposes a general compliance obligation to follow the new standardized KPI disclosure approach whenever preparing draft offer documents and offer documents. Compliance officers should therefore treat this as a mandatory disclosure-standard update affecting all future offer-document preparations by proposed-to-be-listed entities and their registered merchant bankers.

rows.title: Circular on updation of paid up equity capital on a fully diluted basis at Exchange portal
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India’s circular dated **February 28, 2025** (Ref. **NSE/CML/2025/09**) directs **all listed companies / listed entities** to update their **paid-up equity capital** and **paid-up equity capital on a fully diluted basis** on the Exchange’s **NEAPS portal**, measured in terms of the **number of shares**, together with the **conversion ratio** details where applicable. This requirement is linked to SEBI Circular **IMD/FPIC/CIR/P/2018/61 dated April 05, 2018**, which concerns monitoring of foreign investment limits in listed Indian companies.

The key compliance issue addressed by NSE is that companies have **not been updating this information on NEAPS**. As a result, every listed company is now advised to make a **one-time update** on NEAPS **if the information has not already been updated**, **even where there are no outstanding convertible instruments**. After this initial update, companies must continue to **update the same information whenever there is any change** in the paid-up equity capital, diluted capital, or conversion ratio details.

NSE specifies the upload path as **NEAPS > Masters > Paid up Equity capital (Diluted basis)**. The circular does **not set a separate deadline date** or numerical threshold, but it imposes an ongoing procedural obligation to ensure the portal records remain current. Compliance teams should confirm whether the company’s data has been populated correctly and implement a control process to update NEAPS promptly whenever the capital structure changes.

rows.title: Update on single filing system through API-based integration between Stock Exchanges - Integrated Filing (Governance)
rows.summary:
The circular announces an extension of the stock-exchange API-based single filing system to **Integrated Filing (Governance)**, effective **March 1, 2025**, under **NSE/CML/2025/07 dated February 28, 2025**, as an update to the earlier circular **NSE/CML/2024/28 dated September 30, 2024**. From that date, listed entities using the integrated filing framework will be able to submit certain governance-related disclosures once through the connected exchange filing system rather than duplicating the same filing separately on both exchanges.

The circular confirms the filing framework now covers the following disclosures and their applicable timelines/statuses: **Investor Grievance Report under Regulation 13(3)** with an original effective date of **October 1, 2024**, which is stated as **merged with Integrated Filing (Governance) pursuant to the SEBI circular dated December 31, 2024**; **Corporate Governance Report under Regulation 27(2)** with effective date **October 26, 2024**; **Reconciliation of Share Capital Audit Report under Regulation 76** with effective date **November 15, 2024**; and **Meetings of shareholders and voting under Regulation 44(3)** with effective date **December 28, 2024**. It also adds **Integrated Filing (Governance)** for **Regulations 13(3), 27(2), and 30** effective **March 1, 2025**.

The applicability table shows that the single filing system is currently available for certain listed-company categories and not yet for others, with the circular indicating coverage for **equity** and **equity + debt** listed companies for some disclosures, while the entries for **exclusively debt**, **REITs**, and **InvITs** are marked **“shall be communicated later”** where applicable. For compliance purposes, the key operational requirement is that listed entities **should not make multiple filings of the same disclosure on both exchanges** once the single-filing mechanism applies. If one exchange later raises a clarification request after submission, the company must **respond to the same exchange that asked for the clarification**, rather than routing the response elsewhere.

For follow-up, the circular directs companies to use the contact details available on the **NEAPS platform** under **NEAPS > Help > Contact Us > Listing Compliance** for any questions on the subject.

rows.title: Circular on the Industry Standards Note on Regulation 30 of the LODR Regulations
rows.summary:
This circular transmits SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/25 dated February 25, 2025, which introduces an “Industry Standards Note on Regulation 30 of the LODR Regulations” for listed entities. The industry standards were prepared by the Industry Standards Forum (ISF) comprising ASSOCHAM, CII, and FICCI, under the aegis of the stock exchanges and in consultation with SEBI, to support consistent and effective implementation of Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, i.e., the disclosure of material events or information by listed entities.

For compliance teams, the key point is that this is not just informational: SEBI is issuing industry standards that listed entities are expected to use in practice when assessing and making Regulation 30 disclosures. The circular is addressed to all listed entities, all recognized stock exchanges, and the three industry associations, and NSE states that the SEBI circular and the accompanying Industry Standards Note are enclosed for reference and necessary action; the NSE circular itself is dated February 25, 2025 and is available on the NSE website. The document provided does not itself specify a separate compliance deadline, quantitative threshold, or new filing date, but the operative requirement is to align internal materiality/disclosure processes with the industry standards issued for Regulation 30.

In practical terms, any listed company subject to Regulation 30 should review the attached Industry Standards Note and update its internal escalation, assessment, and disclosure procedures accordingly, because the purpose of the standards is to make disclosures of material events/information more uniform and effective across listed entities. Since the circular references “necessary action at your end,” compliance officers should treat this as a prompt to ensure the company’s disclosure policy, authorized signatory/approval workflow, and event-triage process reflect the new industry standards immediately upon receipt.

rows.title: Circular on the Industry Standards on Minimum information to be provided for review of the audit committee and shareholders for approval of a related party transaction.
rows.summary:
This circular communicates that SEBI has issued new **industry standards for the minimum information that must be presented when seeking approval of a related party transaction (RPT)** from the **audit committee** and, where required, from **shareholders**. The SEBI circular is **No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/18 dated February 14, 2025**, and the NSE has circulated it to all listed entities under **Circular Ref. No. NSE/CML/2025/05 dated February 15, 2025**. The change is not a change to the basic approval requirement itself, but a formalization of the **minimum data set and presentation standards** that listed entities must use when placing RPTs before the audit committee and shareholders.

The circular is issued in the context of **Regulations 23(2), 23(3), and 23(4) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (LODR Regulations)**, which already require RPTs to be approved by the audit committee and, in certain cases, by shareholders. SEBI has now published the attached **Industry Standards note on “Minimum information to be provided for review of the audit committee and shareholders for approval of a related party transaction”**, which listed entities are expected to follow when preparing approval materials. For compliance purposes, this means a company should not rely on generic board/audit committee notes for RPT approvals; instead, it must ensure the approval papers contain the specific minimum information prescribed by the industry standard so that the audit committee and shareholders can evaluate the transaction properly.

The circular is addressed to **all listed entities**, and also copied to **all recognized stock exchanges** as well as industry bodies (**ASSOCHAM, FICCI, and CII**), indicating that the standards are intended to be broadly applied across listed companies. The NSE notes that the SEBI circular and the industry standards note are enclosed and also available on the NSE website. No separate implementation timetable, transition period, monetary threshold, or exemption is stated in the text provided, so the operative compliance expectation is that listed entities should **immediately align their RPT approval documentation and internal approval process** with the SEBI-issued industry standards for any audit committee or shareholder approval going forward.

rows.title: Clarification on fixing the record date under Regulation 42 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015
rows.desc: Department: LISTING Circular Ref. No: NSE/CML/2025/04 Date: February 07, 2025 To All Listed Entities, Subject: Clarification on fixing the record date under Regulation 42 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 This is with reference to the recent amendment made by the Securities and Exchange Board of India to regulation 42 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements), Regulations, 2015 vide notification dated December 12, 2024. It is clarified that listed entities shall ensure a minimum gap of at least three working days between the date of board/shareholders’ approval, as applicable to the specific corporate action mentioned in Regulation 42 (1), and the Record Date fixed for such purpose. The minimum gap shall be exclusive of the date of board/shareholder's approval and the actual record date. Further, as per latest amendment, sub-regulation 5 of Regulation 42 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements), Regulations, 2015 has been omitted. Hence the listed entities are not required to announce dates of closure of their transfer books for any purpose. All Listed entities are requested to take note of the same and comply accordingly. For and on behalf of National Stock Exchange of India Limited Senior Manager Harshad Dharod
rows.summary:
This circular clarifies how listed entities must fix a record date under Regulation 42 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, following SEBI’s amendment notified on December 12, 2024. For any corporate action covered by Regulation 42(1), the company must ensure a minimum gap of at least **three working days** between the relevant **board approval or shareholders’ approval date** (whichever applies to that corporate action) and the **record date** fixed for the purpose; this gap is calculated **excluding both the approval date and the actual record date**. In practical terms, compliance teams need to verify that the record date is not set too close to the approval date and that the intervening period consists of at least three working days.

The circular also states that **Regulation 42(5) has been omitted** by the latest SEBI amendment, which means listed entities are **no longer required to announce the dates of closure of their transfer books for any purpose**. This is a substantive process change for listed companies and their compliance/secretarial teams: they should stop issuing transfer-book closure announcements and instead follow the revised record-date framework under Regulation 42. The circular is addressed to **all listed entities** and asks them to take note and comply accordingly, effective in light of the SEBI amendment referenced in the circular dated **February 07, 2025**.

rows.title: Circular for implementation of recommendations of the Expert Committee for facilitating ease of doing business for listed entities- XBRL filing for disclosure of Integrated Filing- Governance
rows.summary:
This circular from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited, dated January 13, 2025, implements part of the SEBI and NSE actions on the Expert Committee recommendations for easier compliance by listed entities, specifically for the **“Integrated Filing – Governance”** disclosure. The key operational change is that the **XBRL utility for Integrated Filing – Governance will be available on NEAPS starting January 14, 2025**, under **Compliance >> Common XBRL Upload >> Integrated Filing >> Integrated Filing – Governance**.

From **January 14, 2025 onward**, **all listed entities must file the Integrated Filing – Governance only in XBRL format and within the prescribed timelines**; the circular expressly states that **PDF disclosure for Integrated Filing – Governance in the Corporate Announcement is no longer required effective that date**. However, listed entities must **continue filing the existing Corporate Governance and Investor Grievance Report in XBRL form under the current process**, and they must do so **alongside the new Integrated Filing – Governance utility and within the new timelines**, until further notice. This means the change is additive in the sense that the new integrated filing obligation starts, but the legacy governance and investor grievance XBRL reporting obligation remains in place for now.

The circular also clarifies that if any listed entity has **already submitted Integrated Filing – Governance in PDF**, it **may still submit the same information in XBRL** as required under the new process. For questions, listed entities are directed to use the contact details on NEAPS (**NEAPS > Help > Contact Us > Listing Compliance**) or email **takeover@nse.co.in**.

rows.title: Circular for implementation of recommendations of the Expert Committee for facilitating ease of doing business for listed entities - Integrated Filing
rows.desc: Non-Confidential Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref No: NSE/CML/2025/02 Date: January 02, 2025 To, The Company Secretaries, All Listed Entities Subject: Implementation of recommendations of the Expert Committee for facilitating ease of doing business for listed entities This has reference to the amendments to the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“SEBI LODR”) which have been published in the Gazette of India on December 13, 2024 and to give effect to certain recommendations of the Expert Committee and carry out consequential changes to the provisions of SEBI Master Circular dated November 11, 2024, on compliance with the SEBI LODR by listed entities, SEBI has issued a circular SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/CIR/P/2024/185 dated December 31, 2024 (‘SEBI Circular’). In this regard a copy of SEBI Circular dated December 31, 2024, is enclosed for your reference and for necessary action at your end. The copy of the circular will also be made available on the NSE website at https://www.nseindia.com/companies- listing/circular-for-listed-companies-equity-market Based on the above, the Integrated Filing shall be applicable for the filings to be done for the quarter ending December 31, 2024, and thereafter. The timelines for Integrated Filing shall be as follows: a. Integrated Filing (Governance): within 30 days from the end of the quarter; b. Integrated Filing (Financial): within 45 days from the end of the quarter, other than the last quarter, and 60 days from the end of the last quarter and the financial year In this regard, the first quarterly Integrated Filing i.e. Integrated Filing (Governance) and Integrated Filing (Financial) which is applicable for the quarter ending December 31, 2024, may be filed within a period of 45 days from the end of the quarter. However, for subsequent quarterly filings, the companies shall follow the timelines as mentioned under point a & b above. Note: Basis the above
rows.summary:
This circular notifies all listed entities that, following amendments to the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 published in the Gazette of India on December 13, 2024, SEBI issued a further circular on December 31, 2024 to implement recommendations of the Expert Committee aimed at easing compliance for listed entities and to make consequential changes to the SEBI Master Circular dated November 11, 2024. The key change is the introduction of **Integrated Filing**, which becomes applicable to filings for the **quarter ended December 31, 2024 and onward**.

For compliance timing, **Integrated Filing (Governance)** must be submitted **within 30 days from the end of each quarter**. **Integrated Filing (Financial)** must be submitted **within 45 days from the end of the quarter** for all quarters **other than the last quarter**, and **within 60 days from the end of the last quarter and the financial year**. For the **first applicable quarterly filing**—covering the quarter ended **December 31, 2024**—both the governance and financial components may be filed together **within 45 days from the quarter-end** as a one-time transition arrangement.

The circular is addressed to **company secretaries of all listed entities**, so it affects all listed companies required to comply with SEBI LODR reporting obligations. The NSE notes that the SEBI circular is enclosed for reference and that it will also be available on the NSE website. The practical compliance action is to adjust internal reporting calendars and processes immediately so that quarterly governance data and financial disclosures are prepared in line with the new integrated filing deadlines, with special attention to the transitional deadline for the quarter ended December 31, 2024.

rows.title: Allowing subscription to the issue of Non-Convertible Securities during trading window closure period
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) circular dated January 1, 2025 is a forwarding/implementation notice to all listed entities, through their company secretaries, drawing attention to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/ISD/ISD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2024/180 dated December 30, 2024, titled “Allowing subscription to the issue of Non-Convertible Securities during trading window closure period.” The NSE notice itself does not add new substantive obligations; it states that the SEBI circular is enclosed, should be read for reference, and requires “necessary action” by recipients, with the circular also made available on the NSE website.

For compliance purposes, the material point is that SEBI has issued a change affecting listed entities that issue or subscribe to non-convertible securities: subscription to such issues is being permitted even during a trading window closure period. This is relevant to listed entities and their insiders/connected persons who would otherwise be restricted by trading window closure rules, and it implies that companies must align their internal insider trading/trading window procedures with the SEBI direction rather than treating the closure period as an absolute bar to participation in non-convertible securities issuances. The document provided here does not state any additional thresholds, rates, or deadlines beyond the SEBI circular date of December 30, 2024 and the NSE forwarding date of January 1, 2025.

rows.title: Update on single filing system through API-based integration between Stock Exchanges- Voting Results
rows.summary:
This circular updates the National Stock Exchange’s single filing system through API-based integration with the other stock exchange and extends that system to cover **“Voting Results of Shareholders Meeting” filings under Regulation 44(3)**, effective **December 28, 2024**. The stated purpose is to allow listed entities to make a **single filing** that is shared through the exchange integration, rather than submitting the same disclosure separately to both exchanges.

The circular also reiterates the current scope of the single-filing arrangement across disclosure types and entity classes. For **Corporate Governance Report (Reg. 27(2))**, the single-filing system is available for **equity-listed** and **equity + debt-listed** companies, while availability for **exclusively debt-listed companies** and **REITs/InvITs** is marked **“shall be communicated later.”** For **Investor Grievance Report (Reg. 13(3))**, the system applies to **equity-listed**, **equity + debt-listed**, and **exclusively debt-listed** entities, with REITs/InvITs again noted as **to be communicated later**. For **Reconciliation of Share Capital Audit Report (Reg. 76)**, the system applies to **equity-listed** and **equity + debt-listed** companies only, and is shown as not applicable to **exclusively debt-listed** entities and **REITs/InvITs**.

From a compliance perspective, the key operational instruction is that listed entities should **avoid multiple filings of the same disclosure on both exchanges** once the single-filing system is in use. If one exchange raises a clarification request after submission, the company must **respond to the same exchange that sought the clarification**, rather than redirecting the response elsewhere. The circular closes by directing companies to seek help through the **NEAPS platform** under **NEAPS > Help > Contact Us > Listing Compliance**, or by email at **takeover@nse.co.in**.

rows.title: Industry Standards Note on Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) Core
rows.summary:
This Industry Standards Note explains how companies must prepare and report the **BRSR Core** under **Regulation 34(2) of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015**, as incorporated through **SEBI Circular SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-SEC-2/P/CIR/2023/122**. It is intended to help reporting entities comply with the mandatory **BRSR Core disclosure requirements** and is to be read together with the **SEBI BRSR Guidance Note** for principle-specific guidance. The note covers **Part A: General Requirements** and **Part B: Attribute-wise requirements**.

A key general requirement is that reporting entities must use **intensity-based calculations** for the following BRSR Core attributes: **GHG Footprint (Attribute 1)**, **Water Footprint (Attribute 2)**, **Energy Footprint (Attribute 3)**, and **Embracing Circularity (Attribute 4)**. Companies are required to report **intensity ratios** in two forms: **revenue-adjusted for Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)** and **output-based intensity**. For the PPP-adjusted revenue calculation, the document states that the **PPP conversion factor for India as of April 2024 is 22.4 INR per international dollar**; this means INR 22.4 had the same purchasing power in India as US$1 in the United States. The formula given is **PPP Adjusted Revenue in USD = Revenue in INR / IMF PPP Conversion Factor**.

The note also explains the underlying PPP methodology: Purchasing Power Parities are currency conversion rates used to equalize purchasing power across countries by accounting for differences in price levels, and the **International Monetary Fund (IMF)** is identified as the source of PPP rates. For compliance purposes, this means entities reporting BRSR Core intensity metrics must ensure their calculations use the specified PPP-based conversion method and the April 2024 India factor where applicable, rather than relying only on nominal exchange-rate conversions.

rows.title: SEBI Circular on Industry Standards Note on Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) Core
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated **December 20, 2024** is addressed to **all listed entities** and simply informs them that SEBI has issued a new circular titled **“Industry Standards on Reporting of BRSR Core”** under reference **SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2024/177** dated **December 20, 2024**. The NSE notice does **not itself create additional obligations or deadlines**; it states that the SEBI circular is enclosed for reference and “necessary action,” and that the circular is available on the NSE website for review.  

For compliance purposes, the practical requirement is that any listed entity subject to **BRSR Core** reporting must review and implement the **industry standards note issued by SEBI** on how BRSR Core is to be reported. Because this document is only an exchange forwarding notice, it does not spell out the substantive reporting changes, thresholds, formats, or timelines itself; those details would need to be taken from the underlying SEBI circular. The only date expressly stated here is the issuance date, **December 20, 2024**.

rows.title: Appointment of Concurrent Auditor by Merchant Bankers for verification of Allotment process in SME IPO’s
rows.summary: The National Stock Exchange of India has directed all merchant bankers involved in SME IPO allotments to appoint a concurrent auditor from the NSE’s empanelled auditors list for every SME IPO allotment, specifically to verify compliance with the allotment procedure and basis of allotment under Regulation 268(4) of the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018. The auditor must issue a certificate confirming that the prescribed allotment process was followed and that the allocation was made by the registrar and transfer agent (RTA) based on the random number generation produced by the Exchange system, which is intended to increase transparency and verify the integrity of the allotment mechanism. The circular also states that the audit fees may be recovered from the issuing company, so merchant bankers and issuers should plan for this cost in the IPO process. This requirement becomes effective for SME IPO allotments from January 01, 2025, and merchant bankers should use only auditors drawn from the NSE empanelled auditor list available at the provided NSE link.

rows.title: Withdrawal of Master Circular on issuance of No Objection Certificate (NOC) for release of 1% of Issue Amount
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSE), through Listing Circular Ref. No. NSE/CML/2024/39 dated November 26, 2024, informed all listed companies that SEBI has issued a circular dated November 21, 2024 withdrawing the earlier Master Circular on issuance of a No Objection Certificate (NOC) for release of 1% of the issue amount. In practical terms, the change is that the prior master circular governing the NOC process for release of 1% of the issue proceeds is no longer in force, and companies should not rely on that withdrawn framework for future compliance actions.

The NSE circular itself does not introduce a new substantive procedure, threshold, or deadline; instead, it serves as an information notice and points listed companies to the SEBI circular for any “necessary action” at their end. The affected entities are all listed companies, particularly those that may have been subject to or relying on the NOC mechanism tied to release of 1% of the issue amount. Compliance teams should verify the SEBI circular text and update internal post-issue monitoring, release-of-proceeds procedures, and any related filing or approval workflows to ensure they reflect the withdrawal and any replacement instructions, if applicable.

rows.title: Relaxation from certain provisions for units allotted to an employee benefit trust for the purpose of a unit based employee benefit scheme, Alignment of timelines for making distribution by InvITs and Format of Quarterly Report and Compliance Certificate – Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs)
rows.summary:
This NSE circular of November 14, 2024, is an implementation notice for SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS-PoD-2/P/CIR/2024/159 dated November 13, 2024, and it is addressed to all Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) and all parties to InvITs. The NSE does not itself add substantive requirements in the text provided; rather, it forwards SEBI’s circular titled “Relaxation from certain provisions for units allotted to an employee benefit trust for the purpose of a unit-based employee benefit scheme, Alignment of timelines for making distribution by InvITs and Format of Quarterly Report and Compliance Certificate – Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs)” and states that a copy is enclosed for reference and necessary action.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that SEBI has issued changes affecting InvITs on three topics: first, a relaxation from certain provisions where units are allotted to an employee benefit trust for a unit-based employee benefit scheme; second, an alignment of the timelines for making distributions by InvITs; and third, a prescribed format for the quarterly report and compliance certificate applicable to InvITs. The circular is directed specifically at InvITs and related parties, so compliance teams for listed or regulated InvIT structures should review the SEBI circular itself to identify the exact relaxation conditions, the revised distribution timeline, and any reporting/certification template or filing requirements.

The NSE notice itself does not provide the operative dates, thresholds, or the detailed procedural changes, and it does not specify any separate NSE deadline beyond the circular date of November 14, 2024 and the referenced SEBI issuance date of November 13, 2024. Accordingly, the practical compliance action is to treat this as a required review-and-implement notice for all affected InvITs: assess whether any employee benefit trust unit issuances fall within the relaxation, update distribution processes to the newly aligned timeline, and ensure quarterly reporting/compliance certificates follow the SEBI-prescribed format.

rows.title: Relaxation from certain provisions for units allotted to an employee benefit trust for the purpose of a unit based employee benefit scheme, Alignment of timelines for making distribution by REITs and Format of Quarterly Report and Compliance Certificate - Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs)
rows.summary:
This NSE circular is a forwarding notice to all Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) and all parties to REITs, dated November 14, 2024, informing them of a SEBI circular issued on November 13, 2024 (SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS-PoD-2/P/CIR/2024/158) titled “Relaxation from certain provisions for units allotted to an employee benefit trust for the purpose of a unit based employee benefit scheme, Alignment of timelines for making distribution by REITs and Format of Quarterly Report and Compliance Certificate - Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs).” The NSE document itself does not set out the substantive rule changes; it states that the SEBI circular is enclosed and requires REITs to take “necessary action” in line with that circular.

From the title and reference, the substantive regulatory changes concern three areas affecting REITs: first, a relaxation from certain provisions where units are allotted to an employee benefit trust for a unit-based employee benefit scheme; second, alignment of the timelines by which REITs must make distributions; and third, a revised format for the quarterly report and compliance certificate. Because the NSE notice is only an intimation and not the operative rule text, it does not specify the exact relaxed provisions, the revised distribution timetable, any numerical thresholds, or the precise reporting format changes. Compliance teams should therefore treat this as a notice that a new SEBI framework has been issued and should review the attached SEBI circular directly to identify the specific obligations, implementation dates, and any filing or certification changes that apply to their REIT and related parties.

rows.title: Update on single filing system through API-based integration between Stock Exchanges
rows.summary:
This circular updates the NSE’s single filing system through API-based integration between stock exchanges and expands it to cover **filings of the Reconciliation of Share Capital Audit Report** under **Regulation 76** of the relevant depository/SEBI framework. The key implementation date is **November 15, 2024**, from which this report can be filed through the single filing mechanism. The circular is addressed to **company secretaries of all listed entities** and applies to the listed-entity categories shown in the table: **equity-only** and **equity+debt** listed companies are covered for Corporate Governance Report filings under **Regulation 27(2)** and Investor Grievance Report filings under **Regulation 13(3)**; **exclusively debt** listed companies are covered for Investor Grievance Report filings, while Corporate Governance Report and some other categories for debt/REITs/InvITs are noted as “shall be communicated later.” For the newly added **Reconciliation of Share Capital Audit Report**, the table shows availability for **equity-only** and **equity+debt** listed companies, and not for exclusively debt, REITs, or InvITs.  

From a compliance perspective, NSE is specifically instructing listed entities to **avoid making duplicate filings of the same disclosure on both exchanges** now that single filing is intended to be operational. If, after a filing is submitted, **any exchange seeks clarification**, the company must respond to **that exchange which requested the clarification**. The circular does not introduce a monetary threshold or penalty, but it does create a procedural obligation to use the single-filing workflow for the specified disclosures and to route post-filing responses to the requesting exchange. For questions, the circular directs entities to the **NEAPS platform** path **NEAPS > Help > Contact Us > Listing Compliance** or to email **takeover@nse.co.in**.

rows.title: Standard Operating Process under SEBI (PIT) Regulations, 2015 for ensuring compliance with Structured Digital Database (“SDD”)
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India issued Circular Ref. No. NSE/CML/2024/35 on November 13, 2024, as a continuation of its earlier circular NSE/CML/2024/31 dated October 18, 2024, to clarify compliance with the Structured Digital Database (“SDD”) requirements under the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015. The circular states that Regulations 3(5) and 3(6) apply not only to listed entities but also to unlisted companies that are being listed pursuant to any scheme approved by the NCLT.  

For such NCLT-scheme listing cases, the company must submit an SDD Certificate from a Practicing Company Secretary (“PCS”) when filing the listing application with the stock exchange, confirming that the company complies with Regulations 3(5) and 3(6) of the SEBI PIT Regulations, 2015, including any amendments to those provisions. The circular does not introduce a numeric threshold or rate, but it does impose a specific procedural compliance obligation: the exchange will expect documentary certification of SDD compliance at the application stage for these entities.  

The circular is effective immediately, so listed entities and entities proposing to be listed under an NCLT-approved scheme should implement or verify their SDD controls and ensure the PCS certificate is available for filing without delay. The Exchange explicitly instructs all listed companies to take note and comply accordingly.

rows.title: Inclusion of Mutual Fund units in the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015
rows.summary:
This NSE circular (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2024/34, dated November 06, 2024) is an intimation to all Asset Management Companies and all Registered Registrar & Share Transfer Agents that SEBI has issued a new circular on October 22, 2024 titled “Inclusion of Mutual Fund units in the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015.” The NSE notice itself does not spell out the substantive rule changes; it serves to forward SEBI’s circular and directs recipients to take “necessary action” in line with that SEBI communication. In practical terms, compliance teams at AMCs and RTAs should treat this as notice that mutual fund units are now being brought within the ambit of the SEBI Insider Trading framework, meaning insider trading controls, compliance procedures, and any related disclosures/restrictions applicable under the SEBI circular must be reviewed and implemented for mutual fund units as required by SEBI.

No separate effective date, transition period, threshold, rate, or deadline is stated in this NSE notice beyond the fact that it is dated November 06, 2024 and references the underlying SEBI circular dated October 22, 2024. The document also notes that the SEBI circular is enclosed and available on the NSE website for reference. For compliance purposes, the key action is to obtain and follow the underlying SEBI circular, because this NSE communication is only the distribution notice and does not itself contain the operational requirements.

rows.title: Circular on update for the single filing system through API-based integration between Stock Exchanges
rows.summary:
This circular updates the earlier NSE circular dated September 30, 2024 on the single filing system via API-based integration between stock exchanges and expands the scope of that system for certain disclosures starting **October 26, 2024**. Specifically, the exchange states that the single filing mechanism is now available for **Corporate Governance Report filings under Regulation 27(2) of SEBI LODR** for **equity-listed companies** and for **Grievance Redressal Mechanism filings under Regulation 13(3)** for **exclusively debt-listed companies**. The circular’s table indicates that for **equity-only** and **equity + debt** listed companies, both of these disclosure types are covered; for **exclusively debt** listed companies, only the grievance redressal mechanism disclosure is covered; and for **REITs and INVITs**, the relevant availability is marked as **“shall be communicated later,”** meaning they are not yet included in this update.

The compliance expectation is that listed entities should **not file the same disclosure multiple times on both exchanges** now that the single filing system is intended to operate for these covered submissions. If, after a disclosure is submitted, one exchange asks for clarification, the company must respond **to the same exchange that requested the clarification** rather than routing the response elsewhere. The circular applies to **all listed entities** receiving the notice, but the operational effect differs by listing category as described above.

For follow-up queries, the circular directs companies to the relevant NSE team contacts in the **NEAPS platform** under **NEAPS > Help > Contact Us > Listing Compliance**, or to email **takeover@nse.co.in**.

rows.title: Circular for fetching of documents from Tax Service Platform available with Depository by Listed Companies for giving tax claim relief to Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) from the perspective of ease of doing business
rows.summary:
This circular informs all listed companies that NSDL has created a Tax Service Platform that lets custodians upload FPI tax-relief documents once per financial year, so issuers and their registrars/transfer agents can fetch them instead of repeatedly collecting the same paperwork from each company. The change is intended to ease operational burden in applying reduced withholding tax on dividend and interest payments made to Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs), since those payments are taxable in shareholders’/bondholders’ hands under the Finance Acts, 2020, 2021, and 2023 amendments to the Income Tax Act.

For compliance purposes, the circular reminds listed entities that tax deducted at source on dividend/interest must be applied at the rate relevant to the shareholder category: domestic investors may be exempt in some cases, while FPIs are generally subject to TDS at 20% plus surcharge and cess, unless a lower treaty rate under a Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA) applies. To claim that beneficial DTAA rate for FPIs, companies normally need supporting documents such as Form 10F, a permanent establishment declaration/document, and a tax residency certificate.

The practical requirement is not a new tax rate or statutory deadline, but a process change: listed companies are requested to take note of and use the NSDL Tax Service Platform to fetch the relevant documents for determining the applicable tax deduction rate when paying dividends or interest to FPIs. The circular is dated October 25, 2024 and is issued by NSE’s Listing Department to all listed entities, so compliance teams and their RTAs/custodians should update their withholding-tax workflows to rely on the platform where available rather than repeatedly requesting the same FPI documentation from each issuer.

rows.title: Standard Operating Process under SEBI (PIT) Regulations, 2015 for ensuring compliance with Structured Digital Database (“SDD”)
rows.summary:
The document is titled as a “Standard Operating Process under SEBI (PIT) Regulations, 2015 for ensuring compliance with Structured Digital Database (SDD),” indicating it is an internal compliance procedure intended to help the organization meet the SEBI Prohibition of Insider Trading framework, specifically the requirement to maintain a Structured Digital Database. However, the text provided appears to be a corrupted/encoded file dump rather than readable document content, so I cannot reliably extract the actual procedural requirements, dates, thresholds, roles, or step-by-step obligations from the body of the document.

For a compliance summary, the only substantive point that can be stated from the visible title is that the document is meant to establish an operating process to ensure SDD compliance under SEBI (PIT) Regulations, 2015. If you can provide a readable version of the document text or the original file contents, I can produce the detailed compliance briefing you requested, including the exact affected entities, recordkeeping/procedure requirements, timelines, and any numerical thresholds or deadlines.

rows.title: Extension of timelines for disclosures by Social Enterprises on Social Stock Exchange ("SSE") for FY 2023-2024
rows.summary:
This circular extends the compliance deadline for **Social Enterprises listed and registered on the Social Stock Exchange (SSE)** to file their **Annual Disclosures** and **Annual Impact Report** for **FY 2023–24**. SEBI had previously set the outer deadline at **October 31, 2024** under **Regulation 91C(1)** and **Regulation 91E(1)** of the **SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (SEBI LODR)**, but SEBI’s **October 7, 2024 circular (SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-1/P/CIR/2024/134)** further extends the filing timeline **up to January 31, 2025**.

The extension applies specifically to the **annual disclosure requirements and annual impact reporting obligations** of **social enterprises on the SSE** for the **financial year 2023–24**. The NSE circular dated **October 8, 2024 (NSE/CML/2024/30)** simply forwards SEBI’s revised deadline to listed and registered Social Enterprises and notes that the SEBI circular is enclosed and also available on the NSE website. Compliance teams should treat **January 31, 2025** as the operative deadline for these FY 2023–24 SSE disclosures unless further updated by SEBI.

The SEBI circular is also addressed more broadly to **all recognized stock exchanges, recognized depositories, SEBI-registered merchant bankers and brokers, SEBI-registered Social Impact Funds, and Self-Regulatory Organizations for Social Impact Assessors**, indicating that market infrastructure participants and intermediaries should be aware of the revised timeline, although the direct filing obligation here rests on the Social Enterprises themselves. No new disclosure content is introduced in this circular; the substantive change is the **extension of time** for filing the already-required reports.

rows.title: Relaxation from compliance with certain provisions of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015–Reg.
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India’s circular dated October 7, 2024 is a forwarding/implementation notice to **all listed entities that have listed specified securities**, advising them of SEBI Circular No. **SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2024/133 dated October 3, 2024** on **“Relaxation from compliance with certain provisions of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015.”** The NSE circular itself does **not** set out the substantive relaxations or new filing requirements; it simply states that SEBI has issued the circular, encloses it for reference, and expects listed entities to take **necessary action at their end** as applicable.

For compliance purposes, the key point in this document is that it applies to **listed entities with specified securities** and points them to the SEBI circular for the actual regulatory relief/grace period/details. No specific thresholds, deadlines, or procedural steps are provided in the NSE notice beyond the date of the SEBI circular (**October 3, 2024**) and the NSE forwarding date (**October 7, 2024**). The document also notes that the SEBI circular is available on the NSE website and is being circulated for information and action, so compliance teams should review the attached SEBI circular directly to determine whether any LODR obligations have been relaxed and whether any entity-specific filings, disclosures, or timelines are affected.

rows.title: Introduction of the single filing system through API-based integration between Stock Exchanges
rows.summary:
NSE has announced the first phase of a **single filing system through API-based integration between stock exchanges**, based on SEBI’s June 26, 2024 consultation paper on easing disclosure compliance and harmonizing ICDR/LODR requirements. Under this phase, **equity-listed companies and companies listed in both equity and debt** on **both NSE and BSE** will be able to file the **Grievance Redressal Mechanism disclosure under Regulation 13(3) of SEBI LODR** at **any one stock exchange only**, with automatic dissemination to the other exchange.

This change becomes effective **from October 1, 2024**, and applies to disclosures for the **quarter ended September 30, 2024**. After filing on one exchange, the listed entity must **ensure that acknowledgments are received from both exchanges**, and as a further precaution must **check that the filing appears on both exchanges’ websites**. The document also makes clear that entities may use this single-filing option not only for the disclosure itself but also for **revisions to that filing** at either exchange.

The rollout is limited in this phase: **exclusively debt-listed companies, REITs, and INVITs are not yet covered** by the API integration for this disclosure and must **continue the existing practice of filing on both exchanges** until a later phase. Likewise, companies listed on only one exchange are not affected by the automatic dissemination arrangement, since the system applies only to entities listed on **both NSE and BSE**.

rows.title: Enforcement action on Merchant Bankers for Market Maker’s non-participation in SME segment
rows.summary:
This NSE circular, dated **September 25, 2024** and addressed **to all Merchant Bankers**, announces an enforcement framework for cases where a **market maker does not participate in the SME segment** as required under **Regulation 261 of the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018**. The circular restates the underlying obligation: the **lead manager(s)/merchant banker must ensure compulsory market making through the SME exchange stockbrokers appointed by the issuer**, and this market making must continue for a **minimum of three years** from the **date of listing of the specified securities** or, if applicable, from the **date of migration from the Main Board under Regulation 276**.

Where non-compliance is identified, NSE will apply **graded action against the Merchant Banker** based on repeated violations for the **same market maker and scrip combination**. On the **first instance**, the Merchant Banker will be **notified of the non-compliance** and sent an **advisory letter** instructing it to **consider appointing a new market maker** for the affected scrip. On the **second instance**, **all ongoing applications involving that Merchant Banker will be put on hold for one month** (with **open IPOs excluded**), and the Merchant Banker will be **directed to appoint a new market maker** for the non-complied scrip. On the **third instance**, the Merchant Banker will be **debarred from taking any new assignments for six months**, while **all ongoing applications will again be kept on hold** except open IPOs, and the matter will be **reported to SEBI**.

For compliance purposes, this means Merchant Bankers handling SME listings must actively monitor whether the issuer-appointed market maker is participating as required, because repeated failures by the same market maker in the same scrip can trigger escalating sanctions on the Merchant Banker itself. The circular does not set a new numeric threshold for market-making performance, but it does establish a clear **three-step enforcement ladder** tied to repeated non-participation events and creates a practical obligation to replace the non-compliant market maker when instructed.

rows.title: Circular for Intimation of credit of Dividend into attached bank accounts of notified parties under Special Court (TORTS) Act 1992
rows.summary:
This circular updates listed entities on a reporting obligation tied to dividend payments made to “notified parties” whose bank accounts have been attached under the Special Court (TORTS) Act, 1992. It is issued by NSE on September 23, 2024 as an addition to NSE Circular Ref. No. NSE/CML/2024/15 dated May 29, 2024, and it specifically relies on a further letter from the Office of the Custodian dated June 12, 2024. The key requirement is that when a listed entity credits an online dividend payment into a bank account belonging to a notified party, the company must identify that the account is attached under the Act and intimate the Office of the Custodian accordingly.

The affected entities are all listed companies that make dividend payments, and the affected bank accounts are those of persons notified under the Special Court (Trial of Offences Relating to Transactions in Securities) Act, 1992 whose accounts have been attached by the Custodian. The Custodian’s letter states that these attached bank accounts are maintained by that office until de-notification, and that all debit and credit entries in the attached accounts are already being intimated to notified parties on a monthly basis. In practical terms, companies and their RTAs/financial operations teams need procedures to flag any dividend credit made to such accounts and ensure prompt communication to the Office of the Custodian, rather than treating the payment as a routine dividend disbursement. No numeric thresholds, rates, or new filing deadlines are specified in the text, but compliance is expected immediately upon application of the circular and in line with the existing attachment/monitoring framework under the Special Court Act.

rows.title: Modification in the Announcement Module on NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS) platform
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSE) has updated the announcement module on the NEAPS platform to align the disclosure subjects with the amended SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (SEBI LODR) and the SEBI circular dated July 13, 2023. This is an addition/modification to NSE Circular Ref. No. NSE/CML/2023/57 dated July 14, 2023, and the change applies to the NEAPS path **NEAPS > COMPLIANCE > Announcements > Announcements/CA**. The effective date for the revised module structure is **September 21, 2024**; all other functionality of the announcement process remains unchanged.

For disclosures under **Regulation 30** read with **Part A of Schedule III of SEBI LODR**, listed entities must now choose from a more specific subject bifurcation in the system: **Regulation 30 - Para A**, **Regulation 30 - Para B**, **REITs/InvITs (as applicable)**, and **Others**. These subjects will then be further categorized according to the headers in **Para A and Para B of Part A of Schedule III**. The practical compliance impact is that listed entities must use the correct, specific subject when filing any disclosure/announcement under Regulation 30 and exercise “abundant precaution” to avoid misclassification or incorrect filing in NEAPS.

rows.title: Enabling T+2 trading of Bonus shares where T is the record date
rows.summary:
This NSE circular, dated September 16, 2024, is addressed to **all listed entities** and **all registered Registrar & Share Transfer Agents (RTA/RTAs)**, and it serves as a notice of SEBI’s same-day circular No. **CIR/CFD/PoD/2024/122** titled **“Enabling T+2 trading of Bonus shares where T is the record date.”** The NSE communication itself does not set out the full operational mechanics, but it clearly points recipients to the attached SEBI circular for **necessary action** and indicates that the change is now formally in force from the SEBI circular date.

For compliance purposes, the material point is that SEBI has enabled **T+2 trading for bonus shares when T is the record date**, meaning the listing, trading, and post-corporate action coordination around bonus issues must align to this shorter two-day timeline rather than a longer processing period. Companies that announce bonus issues and their RTAs must therefore ensure they can complete the required record-date-based processing, entitlement finalization, and market-facing actions within the **T and T+2** framework. The circular does not specify any monetary thresholds or percentage rates in the NSE cover note, and it does not itself impose a separate new filing form or fee; instead, it flags that the operational obligations arise under the referenced SEBI circular and must be implemented by the affected listed entities and RTAs.

rows.title: Disclosure for utilization of issue proceeds for Listed Entities on NSE EMERGE
rows.summary:
NSE has issued Circular NSE/CML/2024/23 dated September 5, 2024 for all listed entities on the NSE EMERGE platform. With immediate effect, any entity listed on NSE EMERGE from April 1, 2023 onward must submit to the stock exchange, along with its financial results, a certificate on utilization of issue proceeds that is certified by the statutory auditor and approved by the listed entity’s Audit Committee. The certificate must be prepared in the format set out in Annexure A and must state, object by object, the amount disclosed in the offer document, the actual amount utilized, any unutilized amount, and any variations from the original disclosed purpose.

This reporting obligation continues until either the issue proceeds have been fully utilized or the stated purpose of the proceeds has been achieved. The circular expressly does not apply where a monitoring agency has already been appointed. If the issue proceeds were raised for investment in subsidiary(ies), the utilization details for those proceeds must be certified by the respective statutory auditor(s) of the subsidiary(ies), not just the parent entity’s auditor.

rows.title: Reporting Forms for Social Enterprises listed and registered on SSE
rows.summary:
The document titled **“Reporting Forms for Social Enterprises listed and registered on SSE”** appears to be an **SSE disclosure circular with reporting formats/forms** for social enterprises that are already **listed and registered on the Social Stock Exchange (SSE)**. The content provided is not legible as plain text because it is embedded in a compressed/binary PDF file, so I cannot reliably extract the actual form fields, filing instructions, deadlines, thresholds, or compliance steps from the raw text shown.  

Because of that limitation, I **cannot safely summarize specific obligations, effective dates, reporting frequencies, or numerical requirements** without risking inaccuracies. What can be said from the title and file name is that the document is intended to prescribe **standardized disclosure/reporting formats** for SSE-listed and SSE-registered social enterprises, so a compliance team should expect it to govern **how these entities must prepare and submit SSE disclosures** and should review the readable PDF directly to identify the exact reporting templates and filing requirements.  

If you upload the readable PDF text or a non-binary copy of the circular, I can produce the kind of detailed compliance summary you requested, including the exact obligations, deadlines, affected entities, and any new procedures.

rows.title: Master Circular for Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs)
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) has issued Circular No. NSE/CML/2024/21 dated June 19, 2024 to all Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) and all parties to InvITs, forwarding SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS-PoD-2/P/CIR/2024/44 dated May 15, 2024, titled “Master Circular for Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs).” The NSE notice itself does not create new substantive requirements; it serves as an information/forwarding circular and states that the SEBI master circular is enclosed “for your reference and for necessary action at your end.” The operative compliance implications therefore come from the SEBI master circular, not from any additional NSE-specific rule change in this document.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that the circular applies to all InvITs and their related parties/participants, and recipients are expected to review the enclosed SEBI master circular and take whatever actions are required under that SEBI framework. No new dates, thresholds, rates, or procedural changes are stated in the NSE cover circular beyond the issuance date of June 19, 2024 and the referenced SEBI circular date of May 15, 2024. The document should be treated as a notice to ensure the enclosed SEBI master circular is implemented and followed, with any specific obligations, deadlines, or reporting requirements to be taken from that SEBI text.

rows.title: Master Circular for Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs)
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India has issued Circular NSE/CML/2024/20 dated June 19, 2024, addressed to all REITs and all parties to REITs, transmitting SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS-PoD-2/P/CIR/2024/43 dated May 15, 2024, titled “Master Circular for Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs).” The NSE circular itself does not introduce new REIT-specific requirements, thresholds, deadlines, or procedural changes; it is a forwarding/notification circular stating that the SEBI master circular is enclosed “for your reference and for necessary action at your end.”  

For compliance purposes, the practical instruction is that REITs and all parties to REIT arrangements should review the SEBI master circular dated May 15, 2024 and ensure any obligations in that circular are implemented. The NSE notice is informational, but it signals that the underlying SEBI master circular is the operative document governing REIT compliance and should be treated as requiring action where applicable.

rows.title: Modification in Framework for Offer for Sale (OFS) of Shares to Employees through Stock Exchange Mechanism
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India issued Circular NSE/CML/2024/19 on June 18, 2024 to all listed companies, referring them to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/MRD/MRD-PoD-3/P/CIR/2024/82 dated June 14, 2024, titled “Modification in Framework for Offer for Sale (OFS) of Shares to Employees through Stock Exchange Mechanism.” The NSE circular itself does not set out the substantive rule changes; it functions as a transmission notice directing listed companies to review and implement SEBI’s June 14, 2024 circular and take “necessary action” as required. The affected entities are all listed companies, specifically in relation to any OFS of shares offered to employees through the stock exchange mechanism.  

From a compliance standpoint, the key point is that SEBI has modified the existing OFS framework for employee share sales, and companies must align their procedures, disclosures, and execution practices with the updated SEBI requirements effective from June 14, 2024 (the date of the SEBI circular referenced by NSE). The NSE notice does not specify any additional thresholds, rates, deadlines, or procedural details beyond directing companies to the enclosed SEBI circular and the NSE website for the operative instructions. Compliance teams should therefore treat the SEBI circular as the controlling source of the new obligations and verify whether any employee-offer OFS transactions planned after June 14, 2024 need to follow revised eligibility, execution, or exchange-mechanism rules.

rows.title: Self Regulatory Organizations for Social Impact Assessors in the context of Social Stock Exchange (“SSE”)
rows.summary: This NSE circular is a transmission notice, not a standalone rule change. On June 5, 2024, the National Stock Exchange of India informed all Social Enterprises, all Recognized Depositories, all SEBI-registered Merchant Bankers and Brokers, and all SEBI-registered Social Impact Funds that SEBI had issued Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2024/0060 dated May 27, 2024 on “Self Regulatory Organizations for Social Impact Assessors in the context of Social Stock Exchange (SSE).” The NSE’s communication does not itself set out the substantive requirements; it directs recipients to the SEBI circular for the actual guidance and says the circular is enclosed and available on the NSE website for “necessary action” as applicable. No effective date, compliance deadline, threshold, fee, or procedural detail is stated in the NSE notice itself. For compliance purposes, the key action is to review the referenced SEBI circular immediately because that document contains the operative requirements for SSE-related social impact assessors and any obligations that may apply to the addressed market participants.

rows.title: Timelines for disclosures by Social Enterprises on Social Stock Exchange ("SSE") for FY 2023-2024
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) is forwarding SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2024/0059 dated May 27, 2024, titled “Timelines for disclosures by Social Enterprises on Social Stock Exchange (SSE) for FY 2023-24,” and advising the addressed market participants to take necessary action accordingly. The NSE circular itself is dated June 5, 2024 and is addressed to all Social Enterprises, all Recognized Depositories, all SEBI-registered Merchant Bankers and Brokers, all SEBI-registered Social Impact Funds, and all Self-Regulatory Organizations for Social Impact Assessors.

This NSE communication does not set out the substantive disclosure deadlines itself; instead, it encloses and points recipients to the underlying SEBI circular for the actual requirements governing FY 2023–24 SSE disclosures. For compliance purposes, the key point is that entities subject to SSE reporting—particularly Social Enterprises and the intermediaries and infrastructure participants named above—must review and follow the timelines and instructions contained in the SEBI circular dated May 27, 2024, as that is the operative regulatory guidance. The NSE notes that the SEBI circular is also available on the NSE website for reference.

rows.title: Announcement submission for Verification of Market Rumours
rows.summary:
This NSE circular, dated June 3, 2024, tells listed companies how to file announcements for verification of market rumours under Regulation 30(11) of the SEBI LODR framework. It refers to SEBI circulars dated May 21, 2024 and the related industry standards note, which made the market-rumour verification requirement applicable first to the top 100 listed entities from June 1, 2024, and then to the top 250 listed entities (meaning the next 150 entities) from December 1, 2024. NSE has now added a specific announcement subject line, **“Rumour verification – Regulation 30(11)”**, which is effective from **June 1, 2024** and must be used for these filings.

The circular also gives the exact filing route in the NEAPS system: **NEAPS > Compliance > Announcements > Announcements/Corporate Action > Create Announcement**. Listed entities required to comply with Regulation 30(11) must use this new subject and this specific path when submitting announcements relating to verification of market rumours. In practical terms, the compliance obligation is not a substantive change to the rumor-verification rule itself, but a procedural requirement to ensure that any such disclosure is routed and tagged correctly through the exchange’s announcement module. The circular concludes by asking listed entities to note the update and comply accordingly.

rows.title: Circular for Intimation of credit of Dividend into attached bank accounts of notified parties under Special Court (TORTS) Act 1992
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India issued this circular on May 29, 2024 to all listed companies’ Company Secretaries/Compliance Officers, based on an April 26, 2024 letter from the Office of the Custodian, Department of Financial Services. The circular requires listed companies to ensure that whenever an online dividend payment is credited to the bank account of a “notified party” under the Special Court (TORTS) Act, 1992, the company must invariably send intimation of that credit to the Custodian’s office. The purpose is to enable the Custodian to take further necessary action in relation to attached bank accounts of such notified parties.

For compliance purposes, this is an ongoing procedural obligation tied specifically to dividend credits, not a general reporting requirement for all payments. The document does not set a separate deadline, threshold, amount, or phased implementation date; the expectation is immediate compliance upon issuance of the circular. Listed companies should therefore have controls in place to identify when dividend disbursements are being made to accounts of notified parties subject to attachment and to notify the Custodian without fail whenever such a credit occurs.

rows.title: Audiovisual (AV) presentation of disclosures made in Public Issue Offer Documents
rows.summary:
NSE Circular NSE/CML/2024/14 dated May 28, 2024, is an intimation to all listed entities and all issuers proposing to list specified securities that they must comply with SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-TPD-1/P/CIR/2024/55 dated May 24, 2024, titled “Audiovisual (AV) presentation of disclosures made in Public Issue Offer Documents.” The NSE circular itself does not set out the detailed operational requirements; it directs recipients to SEBI’s circular, which is made available on the NSE website for reference.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that this is a mandatory compliance communication affecting entities involved in public issue/initial listing processes for specified securities, not a general market-wide notice with separate substantive provisions in the NSE text. No separate deadlines, thresholds, rates, or procedural steps are stated in the NSE circular beyond the instruction to review the referenced SEBI circular and ensure compliance with it. Compliance teams should therefore treat the May 24, 2024 SEBI circular as the controlling source for the actual AV presentation requirements and confirm whether their current public issue disclosure processes need to be updated accordingly.

rows.title: Industry Standards on verification of market rumours
rows.summary:
This NSE circular does not itself create new requirements; it forwards and draws attention to the SEBI circular dated May 21, 2024, titled **“Industry Standards on verification of market rumours.”** The NSE has sent it to **all listed entities** and says the enclosed SEBI circular is for their **reference and necessary action**, with the text also available on the NSE website.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that **listed entities** should review the SEBI-issued industry standards on how market rumours are to be verified and ensure their internal disclosure/escalation processes are aligned with those standards. The NSE notice itself does **not** state the detailed procedural requirements, effective date mechanics, thresholds, or timelines; it only identifies the SEBI circular reference number (**SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2024/52**) and the issue date (**May 21, 2024**). A compliance team should therefore treat this as a prompt to obtain and implement the underlying SEBI circular’s requirements, rather than as a standalone rule change.

rows.title: Framework for considering unaffected price for transactions upon confirmation of market rumour
rows.summary:
This NSE circular does not create a separate exchange-specific regime; it simply forwards SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2024/51 dated May 21, 2024, to all listed entities and asks them to note it and take necessary action. The subject of the referenced SEBI circular is the “Framework for considering unaffected price for transactions upon confirmation of market rumour,” which indicates a compliance framework for pricing transactions when a market rumour has been confirmed. Based on the text provided, the NSE notice itself contains no operational thresholds, no implementation date beyond the May 21, 2024 circular date, and no independent filing or disclosure deadline; those details would be contained in the underlying SEBI circular rather than in this forwarding notice.

For a compliance team, the key point is that all listed entities should review the SEBI circular and determine whether their transaction pricing processes need to incorporate an “unaffected price” concept when dealing with confirmed market rumours. The NSE states that the circular is available on its website and is issued for information and necessary action, so any affected issuer should treat this as a regulatory update requiring internal review of transaction approval, pricing, and disclosure controls.

rows.title: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) - FAQs and General Observations / Guidelines for filing of BRSR
rows.summary:
The NSE circular dated May 10, 2024 reminds listed companies of the BRSR filing requirement under Regulation 34(2)(f) of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 and SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-SEC-2/P/CIR/2023/122 dated July 12, 2023.
